record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: When there are many job types, each with its own speedup function and its own distribution of inherent size, how should servers be allocated across jobs over time?

evidence.quote: In general, it is common that one has many types of jobs, each with a different speedup function and each with a different distribution of inherent size. It is a huge open problem to figure out how to allocate servers to jobs in this setting.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a queueing system with $k$ servers and $J$ distinct job types arriving over time according to independent stochastic arrival processes. Each job type $j \in \{1,\dots,J\}$ is characterized by:

(i) an inherent size distribution $S_j$ (the amount of inherent work a job of type $j$ requires when run on a single server), and

(ii) a speedup function $s_j : \{1,2,\dots,k\} \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$, where $s_j(a)$ is the instantaneous service rate received by a type-$j$ job when allocated $a$ servers (typically $s_j$ is non-decreasing and sublinear, i.e., concave with $s_j(1)=1$).

A scheduling policy dynamically allocates, at every time $t$, the $k$ servers among the jobs currently in the system, with the constraint that the total number of servers allocated does not exceed $k$ and each job receives an integer number of servers. A job of type $j$ assigned $a$ servers completes service after receiving cumulative work equal to its inherent size at rate $s_j(a)$.

Problem: Determine an allocation policy that minimizes the long-run mean response time (mean sojourn time) of jobs in this system, valid for general $J$, general inherent-size distributions $\{S_j\}$, and general (concave) speedup functions $\{s_j\}$. Either characterize an optimal policy explicitly or establish provable approximation/asymptotic optimality guarantees in terms of $(k, J, \{S_j\}, \{s_j\})$ and the arrival rates.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of allocating servers across many job types with heterogeneous speedup functions and size distributions remains open. Recent work has obtained partial results: asymptotically optimal policies have been derived for multiple classes of parallelizable jobs in heavy-traffic and light-traffic scaling regimes (e.g., Least-Parallelizable-First in light load, SERPT-type prioritization in heavy load), and analyses exist for moldable jobs with concave speedups. However, a fully general optimal allocation for arbitrary speedup functions and size distributions has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotically Optimal Scheduling of Multiple Parallelizable Job Classes
status_evidence.snippet: First results on asymptotic optimality when scheduling many classes of parallelizable jobs; optimal policy depends on load regime (LPF vs SERPT).
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: asymptotic optimality results for many classes of parallelizable jobs in different load regimes.

status_evidence.title: On Optimal Server Allocation for Moldable Jobs with Concave Speed-Up
status_evidence.snippet: Studies optimal server allocation for moldable jobs with concave speedup functions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses restricted versions (concave speedup, moldable jobs).

status_evidence.title: Mean field optimal Core Allocation across Malleable jobs
status_evidence.snippet: CAM problem with multiple classes each with a different speedup function; prior work largely limited to one speedup function or narrow classes.
status_evidence.claim: General multi-class CAM problem remains largely open beyond restricted speedup classes.
